html:
SMTO-SKL-0174 — GitHub couldn't find this automation or its run

GUID: 3ae7020c-6b68-5e98-a6a3-bc275aa25471
Slug: github-workflow-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO asked GitHub about an automation (a GitHub Actions workflow) or one of its runs, and GitHub said it couldn't find it. Either the name or number is wrong, or your GitHub account in SMTO isn't allowed to see it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the GitHub project on github.com, select the Actions tab, and find the automation or run you meant. Note its file name (like ci.yml) or run number. A small difference in the name or number is enough for GitHub to report it missing.
  2. Ask the Agent again, giving that exact file name or run number and the project name. With the exact name, the Agent can look up the right automation instead of guessing.
  3. If it still can't be found, ask whoever set up your GitHub Account in Parameter Store to check that its access key includes this project and Actions access. GitHub hides things your access key can't see and reports them as not found.

What success looks like

  • The Agent shows the automation or run's details, such as its status.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your GitHub access in SMTO. Never paste your GitHub access key into a conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GitHub Actions operation (workflow_*) received a 404 for the workflow, run, job or related resource; GitHub also returns 404 when the token cannot see the resource.

What this means

  • A workflow-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404 for its workflow, run or related resource. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • A workflow-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404 for its workflow, run or related resource.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify exact workflow/run identity and Actions permission in the repository.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the exact workflow ID or filename (for example ci.yml) or run ID exists in this repository via the Actions tab or github.workflow_runs. A 404 can also mean the fine-grained token lacks actions:read (actions:write for dispatch/cancel/rerun) or is not scoped to this repository; fix the token on GitHub, then update granted_permissions in the GitHub Account profile in Parameter Store.
  • Verify the exact workflow ID/filename or run ID in this repository and Actions access; 404 can mean inaccessible.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended accessible Actions resource is resolved by an authorized read.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
